The plasma-assisted cases exhibit modest reductions in peak cylinder pressure and HRR, along with improved combustion consistency, confirming more complete oxidation and smoother pressure development. Overall, the Cummins X15N engine testing verified that plasma-assisted reforming reduced methane leaks and improved combustion efficiency under high-speed operating conditions. The reformer demonstrated stable performance across all duty cycles, with reliable electrical operation and no detectable EMI effects on the engine control system. The observed methane reductions, combined with negligible auxiliary power demand, confirm that the technology can be effectively scaled for both stationary and mobile natural-gas engine platforms. Collectively, the AJAX 2802 and Cummins X15N test results demonstrate the potential of plasma fuel reforming as an energy- efficient retrofit approach for reducing methane slip in a variety of natural-gas-powered systems. 3.7 Discussion of Mechanisms and Implications Tests at bench, facility, and engine scales reveal how plasma fuel reforming can improve combustion efficiency and reduce methane slip. Across all test phases, the plasma discharge was shown to partially decompose methane (CH ) into hydrogen (H ), acetylene (C H ), while also 4 2 2 2 generating solid carbon. These reactions occur under non-equilibrium plasma conditions, where high-energy electrons drive dissociation and radical formation without significantly increasing bulk gas temperature. The result is a reformed fuel mixture with altered composition and reactivity that modifies combustion chemistry within the engine. The reformed fuel has several effects on combustion. Hydrogen enrichment, and to a lesser extent acetylene enrichment, increases flame speed and broadens the lean flammability limit, promoting oxidation of unburned hydrocarbons. At the same time, the partial removal of carbon through decomposition reactions slightly reduces the overall lower heating value (LHV) of the fuel. This change decreases the total energy released per cycle, explaining the measured reductions in HRR, peak cylinder pressure (PCP), and gross IMEP (gIMEP) during plasma-assisted operation. Although the total fuel energy content decreases slightly, the enhanced reactivity of the reformate promotes more uniform and complete combustion, thereby reducing unburned methane.
